Anya (Support): Heads-up, customer seeing intermittent 5xxs + very high tail latency (~6-8s) on /v1/completions. They say it reproduces. Before we hand this off to SRE/Eng, please ask them to provide the items below so we can triage quickly.

Anya (Support): Minimal handoff checklist (send these in the ticket):
• Exact root request time (UTC) and approx time window (e.g. 2026-03-16T14:02:00Z ±2m).
• Full request_id(s) and any trace IDs they see. We commonly return both a body field and a header: e.g. body: `{"request_id":"req_1a2b3c4d"}` and header: `x-request-id: req_1a2b3c4d`. If they have a separate trace id from their tracing system, include that too.
• A HAR export (Chrome: DevTools → Network → right-click → Save as HAR with content).
• A minimal curl that reproduces the error (include model, prompt, headers, and all query/body params).
• SDK logs (JS/ Python) around the same time window (we look for `x-request-id`, `request_id`, and any 5xx body).
• If mobile, a short description of how they call the API (mobile SDK, proxy, or server-side) and an exported proxy trace (Charles/Proxyman) if available.

Tom (SRE): +1. If they can provide 2-3 request_ids from different attempts that hit the problem that helps a lot. Also include which region/endpoint they hit and whether they were on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated.

Anya (Support): Example curl to ask for (please copy/paste and run locally, customer should redact API key):
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"hello","max_tokens":32}'
```
Ask them to paste the full curl output (including response headers). We look for `HTTP/1.1 5xx`, response body, and `x-request-id` header.

Priya (Eng): SDK hints — where customers often find the id: 
• JS SDK: `const res = await client.completions.create(...);` then `res.request_id` or `res.headers['x-request-id']` (depending on SDK version).
• Python SDK: `resp = client.completions.create(...)` -> `resp.request_id` or check `resp.headers.get('x-request-id')`.
• Raw HTTP: look at response header `x-request-id` and response JSON `request_id`.

Priya (Eng): Example minimal repro we ask for (one-shot):
1) Exact curl above (replace input/model if needed).
2) If the customer uses streaming, include whether they saw partial tokens then the error.
3) If rate-limited, include client-side concurrency (workers/processes) and sampling of timestamps.

Tom (SRE): If they cant capture HAR, we can often correlate from our logs with: 
• time window (UTC)
• `x-request-id` or `request_id` value
• region/endpoint

ticket-bot: Please attach uploads to the ticket (do not paste large HARs into Slack).

Anya (Support): Important notes to tell customers: 
• Do not share full API keys or any user PII. Redact or replace API keys with `$REDACTED_KEY`.
• If you must share logs that contain user data, provide a redacted copy or a secure link (ticket attachments or S3 pre-signed link).

Tom (SRE): Once we have a couple request_ids and a HAR/curl we can: replay the requests from our staging infra, correlate with kernel/worker logs, and check for KV cache/QPS spikes.

Anya (Support): TL;DR for the customer (paste into message to them):
"Could you send: (1) the exact request_id(s) you saw (both response JSON and `x-request-id` header if present), (2) a HAR or full curl output, (3) SDK logs around the timestamp, and (4) the UTC time window. Please redact API keys and PII. Attach to the ticket or upload to a secure link."

Priya (Eng): Thanks — if you add the request_ids here Ill start the correlation queries once theyre in the ticket.

Anya (Support): Adding this to the ticket now and pinging customer for the items. Will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
